CREDIT DECISION SUMMARY
========================================
Model Assessment: HIGH RISK — likely to default
Estimated Default Probability: 58.6%
Decision Threshold: 50%

IMPORTANT: This is a statistical model score, not a guarantee. The model estimates a 58.6% probability of serious delinquency within two years based on the provided credit data. Actual outcomes depend on many factors not captured by this model.

KEY FACTORS DRIVING THIS ASSESSMENT
========================================

1. NUMBER OF TIMES 30-59 DAYS PAST DUE (RECENT MILD DELINQUENCIES)
   Observed value : 1
   Risk impact    : This factor increases the estimated default risk (+0.503).
   Interpretation : 1 recorded 30-59-day late payment(s). Payment delinquencies are strong indicators of future default.

2. REVOLVING CREDIT UTILIZATION (THE SHARE OF AVAILABLE CREDIT IN USE)
   Observed value : 49.7%
   Risk impact    : This factor increases the estimated default risk (+0.367).
   Interpretation : A utilization of 49.7% means the applicant is using a significant portion of available revolving credit. High utilization is one of the strongest predictors of default risk.

3. APPLICANT AGE
   Observed value : 42
   Risk impact    : This factor increases the estimated default risk (+0.201).
   Interpretation : At 42 years old, the applicant's age is associated with shorter credit history.

RECOURSE RECOMMENDATIONS
========================================
A feasible recourse pathway exists. The following 3 change(s) would reduce the estimated default probability from 58.6% to 37.1% (below the 50% threshold):

  Step 1: Reduce revolving credit utilization (the share of available credit in use)
    Current value : 49.7%
    Target value  : 20.0%
    Action        : Pay down revolving credit balances so total utilization drops from 49.7% to below 20.0%.
  Step 2: Reduce debt-to-income ratio (total monthly debt obligations relative to income)
    Current value : 0.487
    Target value  : 0.3
    Action        : Reduce total monthly debt payments or increase income to bring the debt-to-income ratio from 0.49 to approximately 0.30.
  Step 3: Reduce number of real estate loans or mortgages
    Current value : 2
    Target value  : 0
    Action        : Reduce real estate loans from 2 to 0.

Note: These recommendations are derived from a domain-constrained counterfactual search. All suggested changes are directionally feasible (e.g., paying down debt, increasing income). The model predicts that implementing all steps simultaneously would change the assessment to low risk.
